sources.title: Vispark Lab public model roster
sources.evidence: Live unauthenticated GET identifies vispark/vision-large, owned_by vispark, 1000000 context, text/image/audio/video/file inputs, text output, tools, reasoning and structured outputs. Its created field is metadata, not an explicit availability statement.

sources.title: Vispark Lab deployed API documentation
sources.evidence: The application bundle documents Vision sizes small, medium and large; PDF input, text output, one-million-token context, tool calls, and the exact vispark/vision-large identifier. Continual-learning weights are state returned by the hosted API.

sources.title: Vision AI by Vispark: a foundational Indian multimodal AI
sources.evidence: September 1, 2025 article says the API is available in small, medium and large sizes. It establishes availability by this date, not the first release of the large variant.

sources.title: Vispark timeline and Terms of Service in deployed application
sources.evidence: Timeline distinguishes the August 2022 Vision Telegram bot, May 15, 2024 generic chat launch, and August 29, 2025 Lab launch. It does not date individual sizes. Terms reserve the service and its features to Vispark/licensors and restrict reproduction and distribution.

sources.title: A Culturally Aware Multimodal AI Model
sources.publisher: Vansh Kumar / Journal of Current Trends in Computer Science Research
sources.evidence: The 2024 author paper describes a 175B Vision model and decoder-only Transformer. It does not identify the current large API variant; its historical count is not transferred.

sources.title: A Self-Improving Experiential AI Model: A Path to Continual Learning
sources.publisher: Vansh Kumar and M. Tanusri / Vispark Research Lab
sources.evidence: The November 2025 paper describes 250B Vision Experiential with a Transformer backbone and adaptation components. No large/medium/small mapping or active count is supplied. Later CLv1 disclosures are distinct evidence.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 model specifications and family
sources.evidence: Current developer page names founder Vansh Kumar, links its playground to Vispark Lab, labels the continual-learning core proprietary, and explicitly lists CLv1 550B, Medium 175B and Small 45B. These are nominal author claims, not independently counted checkpoints.

sources.title: Continual Learning Models: An Introduction to Weight Management
sources.evidence: Complete indexed first-party article describes a modified Transformer and 550B base CLv1, and links its ARC-AGI-3 evaluation repository. It distinguishes the base model from returned experience-weight state. Direct HTTP access timed out; the search index supplied the full article, crawled about one month before this audit.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 ARC-AGI-3 evaluation repository
sources.evidence: The evaluation repository linked by the CLv1 article explicitly calls its model Vispark/Vision Large. Its client uses the Vispark Vision endpoint with large size; only the harness and returned state are distributed, not base-model checkpoints.

sources.title: Original Vision Large catalog record
sources.evidence: Upstream comments explicitly derive May 15, 2024 from the model-roster created timestamp. This explains the unsupported release-date interpretation; it is not primary availability evidence.

name.note: The exact roster identifier is vispark/vision-large; remove the provider prefix from its display name.

developer.note: The API identifies Vispark as owner. Later CLv1 material is published by AIVOCO and founder Vansh Kumar and points back to Vispark Lab.

family.note: The documented Vision API has small, medium and large sizes.

release_date.note: Clear May 15, 2024: upstream took it from created metadata for the generic Vision launch. The large API is explicitly available by September 1, 2025, after the August 29 Lab launch, but its earliest availability is unresolved. Neither date is substituted for an exact-variant launch.

open_weights.note: The documented distribution is a hosted proprietary base model. Returned continual-learning state and the MIT evaluation harness are not downloadable base-model weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted base model: the developer calls its core proprietary and reserves service rights. The evaluation harness license does not license model weights.

parameters_b.note: Nominal author-reported 550B for the later CLv1 large deployment: the CLv1 article links an evaluation expressly using Vision Large. This is not a tensor count or a claim about the original 2024 model. Earlier 175B/250B Vision papers are not interchangeable with this current alias.

active_parameters_b.note: No separate active-parameter count for this variant is stated in the examined original and later reports or current family table. Total parameters are not equated with active parameters.

architecture.note: The linked CLv1 technical article explicitly describes a modified Transformer. Dense versus mixture-of-experts structure is not established; no such subtype is inferred from the total count.

context_window.note: The exact live roster reports context_length 1000000, consistent with the shared size-specific API documentation.

modalities.note: The exact roster lists text/image/audio/video/file input and text output; Lab documentation identifies PDF among accepted files.

reasoning.note: The exact roster explicitly lists reasoning in supported_features. This verifies the provider declaration, not an independently benchmarked capability or always-on reasoning mode.

tool_call.note: The exact roster lists tools and the shared Vision request schema accepts function definitions for all three sizes.

description.value: Vispark’s large Vision API model, with text, image, audio, video and PDF input, text output, a one-million-token context window and tool calling.
description.note: Replace comparative marketing language with documented API properties; no performance superiority claim is retained.

patch.notes: The 550B count is a nominal developer claim for the later CLv1 large deployment, linked to Vision Large through the developer’s evaluation repository; it is not a measured checkpoint count or a specification for the 2024 model. The CLv1 article describes a modified Transformer but does not establish dense/MoE structure or an active-parameter count. Its complete indexed text was accessible although direct requests timed out. Original Vision and Vision Experiential papers report earlier 175B and 250B models. The catalog release date was derived from created metadata for generic Vision and has been cleared; the large API was explicitly available by September 1, 2025, but its earliest release remains unverified. Returned learning-state blobs and the open evaluation harness do not make base weights open. Capabilities reflect current provider documentation, not an inference test.

summary: Confirms current Vision Large API properties and adds Vision family, proprietary classification, nominal 550B CLv1 total and Transformer architecture using later first-party material and its explicit Vision Large evaluation mapping. Clears the created-timestamp-derived release date. Active count, dense/MoE subtype and earliest exact-variant availability remain unresolved.
